comment: st_56bd10d1 — deterministic source-account/domain → topic routing for GENERAL content classification (chunks.topic for email/chat, wired ahead of the cosine-similarity reclassifier in scripts/ingest/05-reclassify-chunks.js and the initial placement in lib/chunk-worker.js chunkEmails()). Deliberately a SEPARATE file from config/asana-routing.json, which stays scoped to transcript-derived Asana call-task routing per its own header comment — reusing it here would silently broaden a contract that file and its one consumer (lib/call-routing.js) document narrowly. `domains` maps an email/account domain (subdomains included, matched via the shared topicForEmailDomain() matcher in lib/asana-routing-config.js) to a topic slug. A new domain is one row — no code change. PUBLIC-SAFE DEFAULT: this tracked file ships only the universal free-mail default, the product's own domain, and synthetic example rows (acme-corp.example, example-university.edu) that demonstrate the business-domain and education-domain mechanisms. Every owner-identifying venture/employer/education domain lives ONLY in the gitignored config/source-topic-routing.user.json override, merged over this file at load (override wins per key); replace the example rows with your own, or add them via the override. Resolution order (lib/topic-source-routing.js topicForSourceAccount): the MAILBOX account's own domain wins outright whenever it resolves to anything other than the personal default (a dedicated business inbox keeps its own identity even when a message inside it happens to be from an unrelated configured domain); the message's SENDER domain is checked next, which is what lets a configured education-domain sender re-home academic mail that lands inside the general-purpose personal free-mail account; unmatched falls through to the T1-residual queue, then cosine similarity.
